mainTopic: The names of הר סיני, the verse behind the scarlet strip and the אגדה of the אבות, and a new משנה on the amounts for carrying wood, spices, dyes and cleaners on שבת
overview: This amud opens at the end of a list explaining the names of the desert around סיני. It closes that list with a מחלוקת over whether the mountain's real name is חורב or סיני. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about the scarlet strip and explains the verse ״אם יהיו חטאיכם כשנים״. רבי יצחק reads ״כשנים״ as 'like the years', and רבא tells how in the future ישראל find no defender among the אבות and turn to הקב״ה, who whitens their sins. A related אגדה follows: אברהם and יעקב do not defend ישראל, but יצחק argues for them, cuts down the count of their sins, and offers his own merit, and then points them to הקב״ה as their true Father. After a short statement that יעקב's merit spared him from going down to מצרים in chains, a new משנה returns to the minimum amounts for carrying on שבת. The גמרא explains why the amount for wood is not repeated, and then begins a contradiction about spices combining that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the deserts are called פארן and סיני
steps.stepSummary: Finishing a list of the desert's names: פארן because ישראל multiplied there, and סיני because hatred came down on the nations there.
steps.simpleTranslation: [It is called מדבר פארן] because ישראל were fruitful and multiplied there. It is called מדבר סיני because hatred came down upon the nations of the world there.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the גמרא in the middle of a list that explains each name of the desert where the תורה was given. These are the last two names on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name is read as a hint to something that happened there. פארן sounds like פרו (they multiplied). סיני sounds like שנאה (hatred), because the nations who rejected the תורה became hated there.
steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins mid-sentence. The first phrase belongs to the name מדבר פארן, which appeared on the previous amud.

phrases.english: [Paran] — because Israel were fruitful and multiplied on it;
phrases.notes: A play on words: פארן sounds like פרו, "were fruitful."

phrases.english: the Sinai Desert —
because hatred descended upon the nations of the world on it.
phrases.notes: A play on words: סיני sounds like שנאה, "hatred."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a list of names begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names פארן and סיני hint at ישראל multiplying and at the nations becoming hated.

steps.title: The mountain's real name is חורב
steps.stepSummary: After all the nicknames, what is the mountain's actual name? Answer: חורב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is its real name? Its name is חורב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which of all these names is the mountain's true name, and answers that it is חורב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list so far gave reasons for many names. Now the גמרא separates the 'real' name from the descriptive ones. This view treats סיני as just a description and חורב as the true name.

keyTerms.meaning: Horeb, another name for the mountain

phrases.english: And what is its [real] name?
Horeb is its name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the list by identifying the true name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mountain's true name is חורב.

steps.title: רבי אבהו disagrees: the real name is סיני
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says the true name is הר סיני. It is called חורב because destruction (חורבה) came down on the nations there.
steps.simpleTranslation: This argues with רבי אבהו, because רבי אבהו said: its name is הר סיני. Why is it called הר חורב? Because destruction came down upon the nations of the world there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that the last statement argues with רבי אבהו. רבי אבהו holds the opposite: סיני is the real name and חורב is the descriptive one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two views simply flip which name is real and which is a nickname. רבי אבהו also gives a wordplay for חורב: it hints at חורבה (destruction) for the nations who rejected the תורה.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת about which name is the mountain's 'real' one. The first view says חורב, and רבי אבהו says סיני. Each side explains the other name as a hint to what happened to the nations there.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Abbahu,
for Rabbi Abbahu said:
Mount Sinai is its name.
And why is it called Mount Horeb?
Because destruction descended upon the nations of the world on it.
phrases.notes: A play on words: חורב sounds like חורבה, "destruction."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opposing view to step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אבהו, the true name is סיני, and חורב hints at destruction for the nations.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about the scarlet strip
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: where do we learn that a strip of scarlet wool is tied (to the שעיר המשתלח)?
steps.simpleTranslation: [We learned in the משנה:] From where do we know that we tie a strip of scarlet wool, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה so that it can discuss it. This is a setup line that prepares for the questions about the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה brought ״אם יהיו חטאיכם כשנים כשלג ילבינו״ as the hint for tying a scarlet strip. The strip turned white to show that the sins were forgiven. The גמרא now studies that verse closely.

phrases.english: From where is it derived that one ties
a strip of scarlet wool, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: returns from the Sinai discussion to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה derives tying the scarlet strip from ישעיהו א:יח.

steps.title: Why the plural word ״כשנים״?
steps.stepSummary: The verse says ״כשנים״ (plural). It should have said ״כשני״ (singular, 'like scarlet').
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does it say ״כשנים״? It should have said ״כשני״!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a strange word in the verse. The color scarlet is normally שני, so why add the plural ending?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a challenge about wording. An extra letter in a פסוק is taken as a hint that it is teaching something more. The question sets up a דרשה.

phrases.english: "Kashanim" (plural)?
It should have said "kashani" (singular)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the verse cited by the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plural form ״כשנים״ in ישעיהו א:יח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The color is normally written in the singular, so the plural seems extra.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: sins as many as the years since Creation
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reads ״כשנים״ as 'like the years': even if your sins are as many as all the years since Creation, they will become white like snow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: הקב״ה told ישראל: even if your sins are as many as these years that have gone on in order from the six days of Creation until now, they will become white like snow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question by reading שנים as 'years' instead of 'scarlet'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural is a hint to quantity. No matter how many sins have built up, even as many as all the years in history, they can still be made white like snow.

keyTerms.meaning: they will become white like snow

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel:
If your sins are like these years
that proceed continuously
from the six days of Creation until now —
they will become white like snow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural seemed like an unexplained extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural teaches that even countless sins can be cleansed.

steps.title: רבא's questions on ״לכו נא״ and ״יאמר ה׳״
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about the start of the same verse. Why ״לכו נא״ ('go') instead of ״בואו נא״ ('come')? And why the future tense ״יאמר ה׳״ instead of ״אמר ה׳״?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: what does the verse mean, ״Go please, and let us reason together, ה׳ will say״? Why 'go'? It should say 'come'! Why 'will say'? It should say 'said'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises two wording problems in the verse. This step sets up his דרשה, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If הקב״ה invites ישראל to argue with Him, He should say 'come to Me', not 'go'. A prophecy usually says 'ה׳ said', so the future tense is also strange. Both oddities point to a future scene.

keyTerms.meaning: what is [the meaning of] what is written
and let us reason / argue together

phrases.english: Rava taught: What is the meaning of what is written:
"Go please and let us reason together, the Lord will say"?
"Go please"? It should have said "Come please"!
"The Lord will say"? It should have said "The Lord said"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching on the same verse, this time on its opening words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words ״לכו נא״ and ״יאמר״ in ישעיהו א:יח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Go' fits sending someone away, not an invitation. The future tense does not fit a normal prophecy.

steps.title: In the future: go to your fathers to be rebuked
steps.stepSummary: In the future, הקב״ה will tell ישראל, 'Go to your fathers and let them rebuke you.' That explains both 'go' and 'will say'.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the future, הקב״ה will say to ישראל: Go please to your fathers, and let them rebuke you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers both questions with one picture. The verse describes something הקב״ה will say in the future, sending ישראל away to the אבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Will say' means it has not happened yet; it is לעתיד לבא. 'Go' means ישראל are sent somewhere else. They go to the אבות, who will judge them. ונוכחה is read as 'let them rebuke you'.

phrases.english: In the future to come,

phrases.aramaic: יֹאמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, will say to Israel:
Go please to your fathers
and they will rebuke you.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא יֹאמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both wording questions of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Placing the verse in a future scene
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse seemed to be an invitation made in the past.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse describes a future command: go to the אבות for rebuke.

steps.title: ישראל reply: none of the אבות prayed for us
steps.stepSummary: ישראל answer that none of the אבות asked for mercy for them: not אברהם after the prophecy of exile, not יצחק when he blessed עשו, and not יעקב when he went down to מצרים. So they say, 'Now ה׳ will say.'
steps.simpleTranslation: ישראל will say before Him: Master of the World, to whom should we go? To אברהם, to whom You said 'Know for certain [your children will be strangers and slaves],' and he did not ask mercy for us? To יצחק, who blessed עשו 'when you break loose [you will throw off his yoke],' and he did not ask mercy for us? To יעקב, to whom You said 'I will go down with you to Egypt,' and he did not ask mercy for us? To whom shall we go? Now let ה׳ say!
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. ישראל go through each of the אבות and show that none of them stood up for them. So they turn back to הקב״ה Himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each אב heard about a coming suffering and stayed silent. This explains the ending ״יאמר ה׳״: since no אב will defend them, only הקב״ה is left to decide. It sets up His merciful answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: know for certain (בראשית טו:יג, the prophecy of exile)
when you break loose (יצחק's blessing to עשו)

phrases.english: And they will say before Him:

phrases.aramaic: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם אֵצֶל מִי נֵלֵךְ?
phrases.english: Master of the Universe, to whom shall we go?
To Abraham, to whom You said "Know certainly,"
and he did not ask for mercy on our behalf?!
To Isaac, who blessed Esau
"And it shall be when you break loose,"
and he did not ask for mercy on our behalf?!
To Jacob, to whom You said
"I will go down with you to Egypt,"
and he did not ask for mercy on our behalf?!
To whom shall we go?
Now — "the Lord will say."
phrases.notes: Explains the end of the verse: let ה׳ Himself decide.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֹאמְרוּ לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם אֵצֶל מִי נֵלֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's story with ישראל's reply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: None of the אבות pleaded for ישראל, so ישראל turn to הקב״ה alone.

steps.title: Because you relied on Me, your sins will be white as snow
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה answers: since you have placed yourselves in My hands, even sins like scarlet will become white like snow.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקב״ה said to them: Since you have made yourselves depend on Me, 'If your sins are like scarlet, they will become white like snow.'
steps.whatsHappening: This ends רבא's story. When ישראל rely only on הקב״ה, He forgives them completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full verse now reads as one story: 'go' to the אבות, they will not defend you, so 'ה׳ will say', and He makes your sins white. Turning fully to הקב״ה is itself what brings forgiveness. This ties back to the scarlet strip in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: you have made yourselves depend on Me

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of ישעיהו א:יח. רבי יצחק says even countless sins can be whitened. רבא says that when ישראל find no defender among the אבות and rely only on הקב״ה, He whitens their sins.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains the meaning behind the scarlet strip of the שעיר המשתלח: complete forgiveness that comes from turning to הקב״ה.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them:
Since you have made yourselves dependent on Me —
"If your sins be like scarlet,
they will become white like snow."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story with הקב״ה's answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Relying fully on הקב״ה brings complete forgiveness, as the verse promises.

steps.title: What does ״כי אתה אבינו״ mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני, quoting רבי יונתן, asks about ישעיהו סג:טז: 'You are our Father, for אברהם does not know us and ישראל does not recognize us.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: What does the verse mean, 'For You are our Father, for אברהם does not know us and ישראל does not recognize us; You, ה׳, are our Father, our Redeemer, Your name is forever'?
steps.whatsHappening: A related teaching begins, about how the אבות respond to ישראל's sins. This step only quotes the verse, which sets up the story that explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says אברהם and ישראל (יעקב) do not 'know' us, while הקב״ה is our Father. The question is why the אבות would disown ישראל. The coming story answers it and fits well with רבא's story just before.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Yonatan said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"For You are our Father,
for Abraham knows us not,
and Israel does not acknowledge us;
You, Lord, are our Father, our Redeemer,
everlasting is Your name"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, related teaching about the אבות and ישראל's sins.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the verse say the אבות do not know ישראל, while הקב״ה is their Father?

steps.title: אברהם answers: let them be wiped out
steps.stepSummary: In the future, הקב״ה tells אברהם that his children sinned. אברהם answers, 'Let them be erased for the sanctity of Your name.'
steps.simpleTranslation: In the future, הקב״ה will say to אברהם: Your children sinned against Me. He will answer: Master of the World, let them be wiped out for the holiness of Your name.
steps.whatsHappening: The story explaining the verse begins. אברהם is told first, and he does not defend ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains 'אברהם does not know us'. Instead of pleading for them, אברהם puts כבוד שמים ahead of his children.

phrases.english: In the future to come,

phrases.aramaic: יֹאמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְאַבְרָהָם:
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, will say to Abraham:
Your children have sinned against Me.
He says before Him: Master of the Universe,
let them be eradicated for the sanctification of Your name.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעָתִיד לָבֹא יֹאמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְאַבְרָהָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אברהם does not defend ישראל, which explains 'אברהם does not know us'.

steps.title: יעקב also fails to defend them
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה turns to יעקב, who knew the pain of raising children, hoping he will pray for them. יעקב gives the same harsh answer, and הקב״ה says: no sense in the old and no wisdom in the young.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I will tell יעקב, who had the pain of raising children; maybe he will ask mercy for them. He said to him: Your children sinned. He answered: Master of the World, let them be wiped out for the holiness of Your name. He said: there is no sense in the old and no wisdom in the young.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. הקב״ה tries יעקב next, but יעקב also does not defend ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב suffered while raising his children, so he should have felt their pain, yet he answers like אברהם. This explains 'ישראל (יעקב) does not recognize us'. הקב״ה's remark criticizes both: neither the elder (אברהם) nor the younger (יעקב) gave a proper answer.

keyTerms.meaning: that he will ask for mercy

phrases.english: He said: I will say it to Jacob,
who had the pain of raising children;
perhaps he will ask for mercy on their behalf.
He said to him: Your children have sinned.
He says before Him: Master of the Universe,
let them be eradicated for the sanctification of Your name.
He said: There is no reason in elders
and no wisdom in youngsters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: הקב״ה turns from אברהם to יעקב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יעקב also does not defend ישראל, which explains 'ישראל does not recognize us'.

steps.title: יצחק begins to defend: they are Your children too
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה tells יצחק that his children sinned. יצחק pushes back: are they only my children and not Yours? At סיני You called them 'My firstborn son' when they said נעשה before נשמע!
steps.simpleTranslation: He says to יצחק: Your children sinned against Me. He answers: Master of the World, are they my children and not Your children? When they put 'we will do' before 'we will listen', You called them 'My son, My firstborn.' Now they are my children and not Yours?!
steps.whatsHappening: The story turns around. יצחק, unlike the others, starts to defend ישראל. His defense continues in steps 15 and 16, and the story ends in step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יצחק challenges how הקב״ה described them: 'your children'. At קבלת התורה, ישראל earned the title בני בכורי by saying נעשה ונשמע. A father does not disown his firstborn when the child sins.

keyTerms.meaning: my children and not Your children?

steps.confusionAlert: The verse in step 11 names אברהם and ישראל (יעקב) as not knowing us, but not יצחק. That is exactly why יצחק is the one who defends ישראל here.

phrases.english: He says to Isaac:
Your children have sinned against Me.
He says before Him: Master of the Universe,
are they my children and not Your children?!
At the time when they put first before You
"We will do" before "We will listen,"
You called them "My son, My firstborn";
now they are my children and not Your children?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֹמֵר לוֹ לְיִצְחָק: בָּנֶיךָ חָטְאוּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story turns: unlike אברהם and יעקב, יצחק defends ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יצחק argues that ישראל are הקב״ה's own children, His firstborn since נעשה ונשמע.

steps.title: יצחק calculates how few years of sin are really left
steps.stepSummary: יצחק argues that ישראל's sins are limited: from 70 years he subtracts the first twenty, the nights, and time spent praying, eating and in the bathroom. Only twelve and a half years remain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And besides, how much did they really sin? A person lives seventy years. Take away the first twenty, since You do not punish for them, and fifty are left. Take away twenty-five years of nights, and twenty-five are left. Take away twelve and a half years of praying, eating and using the bathroom, and twelve and a half are left.
steps.whatsHappening: יצחק keeps defending ישראל. He does math to show that the time in which they could have sinned is much smaller than it looks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 יצחק argued that ישראל are also God's children. Now he adds a second argument (וְעוֹד): even the amount of sin is small. Each subtraction removes time in which a person is either not punished (under twenty) or is busy with things that are not sin (sleeping, praying, eating, bathroom).

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; adds a second argument

steps.confusionAlert: 'Twenty years You do not punish for' means punishment from heaven (בית דין של מעלה), which begins at age twenty. It does not mean that a person under twenty is not obligated in מצוות.

phrases.english: And furthermore, how much did they sin?
How many are the years of a person?
Seventy years.
Subtract twenty, for which You do not punish
phrases.notes: Heavenly punishment starts at age twenty

phrases.english: Fifty remain for them.
Subtract twenty-five years of nights
Twenty-five remain for them.
Subtract twelve and a half
of praying, eating, and the bathroom
Twelve and a half remain for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second defense argument to יצחק's claim in step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only twelve and a half years of a person's life are really open to sin

steps.title: יצחק offers to share or carry the sins himself
steps.stepSummary: יצחק asks הקב״ה to forgive everything. If not, they should split it. If the whole burden falls on יצחק, he already offered himself as a sacrifice.
steps.simpleTranslation: If You can bear all of them, good. If not, half is on me and half on You. And if You say all of them are on me, I already offered my life before You.
steps.whatsHappening: יצחק finishes his defense with a three-level offer for handling the remaining sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offer goes step by step: full forgiveness, then a 50/50 split, then יצחק taking everything. The final level rests on the עקידה. יצחק already gave his life to God, so that merit can cover his children's sins.

keyTerms.meaning: I offered my life (at the עקידה)

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַתָּה סוֹבֵל אֶת כּוּלָּם — מוּטָב,
phrases.english: If You bear all of them, good;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — פַּלְגָא עֲלַי וּפַלְגָא עֲלָיךְ.
phrases.english: and if not, half on me and half on You.
And if You say all of them are on me,
I already offered my life before You.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the reduced count from step 15 to offer a way to settle the remaining sins
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יצחק offers his own merit from the עקידה to cover ישראל's sins

steps.title: יצחק points the people to הקב״ה as their true Father
steps.stepSummary: ישראל praise יצחק with 'You are our father.' יצחק redirects them to praise הקב״ה. They lift their eyes and say, 'You, ה׳, are our Father.' This explains the פסוק from step 11.
steps.simpleTranslation: They begin and say: 'For you are our father.' יצחק tells them: Instead of praising me, praise הקב״ה. יצחק points to הקב״ה with his eyes. At once they lift their eyes upward and say: 'You, ה׳, are our Father, our Redeemer; Your name is from forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The אגדה ends here. It explains the פסוק in ישעיהו that רבי שמואל בר נחמני asked about in step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם and יעקב did not defend ישראל, so the people think יצחק is the 'father' who cares for them. יצחק sends that praise up to הקב״ה. This is how the פסוק ends with 'You, ה׳, are our Father.'
steps.whatToRemember: The 'father' who saves ישראל is not אברהם or יעקב, and in the end not even יצחק. It is הקב״ה. יצחק only points the way.

phrases.english: They begin and say: 'For you are our father.'
Isaac says to them:
Instead of praising me,
praise the Holy One, Blessed be He.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַחְוֵי לְהוּ יִצְחָק לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בְּעֵינֵיהּ.
phrases.english: And Isaac points out the Holy One, Blessed be He, to them with his eyes.
Immediately they lift their eyes on high and say:
'You, Lord, are our Father, our Redeemer; everlasting is Your name.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the אגדה and completes the explanation of the פסוק raised in step 11
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק 'You are our Father' refers to הקב״ה, to whom יצחק directs ישראל's praise

steps.title: יעקב's merit spared him from going down to מצרים in chains
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says יעקב deserved to go down to מצרים in iron chains, like an exile. His merit let him go gently, as the פסוק in הושע describes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: יעקב אבינו deserved to go down to מצרים in iron chains, but his merit caused him to go gently, as it is written: 'With cords of man I drew them, with bands of love; I was to them like those who lift the yoke off their jaws, and I fed them gently.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבא's aggadah mentioned יעקב going down to מצרים (step 9), the גמרא adds a related statement about how that descent happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזירה told to אברהם was that his descendants would be exiled. Normally exile means being dragged in chains. Because of יעקב's merit, the 'chains' became 'cords of love': out of love he was drawn down with ropes, not chains.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Our father Jacob deserved
to go down to Egypt in iron chains,
but his merit caused it for him (to go gently),
as it is written: 'With cords of man I drew them,
with ropes of love,

phrases.aramaic: וָאֶהְיֶה לָהֶם כִּמְרִימֵי עֹל עַל לְחֵיהֶם
phrases.english: and I was to them like those who lift the yoke off their jaws,
and I fed them gently.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related אגדה statement about יעקב, added by association
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יעקב's merit turned a harsh exile into a gentle descent

steps.title: New משנה on amounts for carrying wood, spices, dyes and cleaners
steps.stepSummary: The משנה returns to the הלכות of carrying on שבת. Wood and spices are measured by cooking or seasoning an easy egg, and spices combine. Dye materials are measured by dyeing a small cloth for a hairnet. Laundry materials are measured by washing that cloth. רבי יהודה says: enough to remove a stain.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who carries out wood is liable for enough to cook an easy egg. Spices: enough to season an easy egg, and different spices join together. Nut shells, pomegranate peels, safflower and madder: enough to dye a small cloth for the opening of a hairnet. Urine, natron, בורית, cimolian earth and potash: enough to wash a small cloth for the opening of a hairnet. רבי יהודה says: enough to remove a stain.
steps.whatsHappening: After the long אגדה, the משנה goes back to the main topic. It lists more items and the minimum amount for which carrying them out on שבת makes a person liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item's amount is set by its normal use. Wood is used for fuel, so the amount is enough to cook. Dyes are used for dyeing, so the amount is enough to dye. רבי יהודה disagrees only about the laundry materials and sets a smaller amount: enough to remove one stain.

keyTerms.meaning: One who carries out (from one domain to another)
They combine to make the amount

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the general rule of הוצאה: liability depends on carrying an amount that is significant for the item's usual purpose.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who carries out wood
(is liable for) enough to cook an easy egg.
Spices: enough to season an easy egg.
And they combine with one another.
Nut shells, pomegranate peels,
safflower and madder

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לִצְבּוֹעַ בָּהֶן בֶּגֶד קָטָן פִּי סְבָכָה.
phrases.english: enough to dye with them a small cloth for the opening of a hairnet.
Urine, natron and borit,
cimolian earth and potash

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לְכַבֵּס בֶּגֶד קָטָן פִּי סְבָכָה,
phrases.english: enough to launder a small cloth for the opening of a hairnet.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי לְהַעֲבִיר אֶת הַכֶּתֶם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: enough to remove a stain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadah and resumes the הלכות of הוצאה on שבת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability amounts are set by each item's typical use: cooking or seasoning an easy egg, dyeing or washing a small hairnet cloth (רבי יהודה: removing a stain)

steps.title: Didn't we already learn the amount for wood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the amount for wood seems repeated. An earlier משנה already said that a thick or broken reed is measured by enough to cook an easy egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned this once! A reed: enough to make a quill. If it was thick or crushed: enough to cook the easiest of eggs, beaten and placed in a pot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first line of the משנה. It points to an earlier משנה that seems to teach the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thick or crushed reed is useless for writing, so it is basically firewood. The earlier משנה already gave its amount as enough to cook an egg. So why does our משנה need to teach the amount for wood again?

phrases.english: GEMARA: We already learned it once!
A reed: enough to make a quill;
if it was thick or crushed,
enough to cook the easiest of eggs,
beaten and placed in a pot.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule seems redundant, since the earlier משנה about a crushed reed already set this amount

steps.title: Wood needed its own ruling because it could serve as a key tooth
steps.stepSummary: The reed case could not teach us about wood. A crushed reed is good for nothing but fuel, but wood can be carved into a key tooth, so we might have thought any amount of wood counts. The משנה teaches that wood is measured as fuel.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: there (the reed), it is not fit for anything else. But wood, which is fit for a key tooth, should count even in any tiny amount. So the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains why the rule for wood is not repeated after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'mistaken thought' (הוה אמינא) is that wood's other use, a key tooth, makes even a tiny piece significant. The משנה rejects this. Wood is normally used for burning, so it is measured by the cooking amount.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (a mistaken assumption)

steps.whatToRemember: An item is measured by its usual, main use. Wood is used for fuel, not for making key teeth, so its amount is enough to cook an easy egg.

phrases.english: You might have said:
There it is not fit for anything (else),
but wood, which is fit for the tooth of a key,
(should be liable) even for any amount;
it teaches us (that it is not so).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the redundancy challenge of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (צריכותא): wood has another possible use that the reed does not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since wood can be a key tooth, even a tiny amount should make one liable
steps.terutzMaskana: Wood is measured by its main use as fuel: enough to cook an easy egg

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's Rule for Spices
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה that the amount for spices is enough to season an easy egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: Spices: enough to season an easily-cooked egg.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from our משנה so it can raise a question on it. This is a setup step that prepares the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה line also said that different spices combine to reach this amount. The גמרא brings this line back into focus because it is about to compare it with a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'easy' egg, one that cooks or seasons easily (a small, light amount)

phrases.english: Spices: enough to season an easily-cooked egg.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. The משנה also said that spices combine with one another.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: קשיא (as the opening of the contradiction)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 21 finished with the wood amount. The גמרא now moves to the next item in the משנה, spices.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For carrying on שבת, the amount for spices is enough to season an easy egg, and different spices combine.

steps.title: A Contradiction from the Law of Forbidden Spices
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets against our משנה a source saying that forbidden spices, from different prohibitions or different species, combine. It then begins to quote חזקיה's explanation of that source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it raises a contradiction: Spices that carry two or three prohibitions, all from one species, or that come from three species with one prohibition, are forbidden, and they combine with each other. And חזקיה said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different source, from the laws of forbidden foods, that also talks about spices combining. It sets that source against our משנה. This passage ends just as the גמרא begins quoting חזקיה, whose words will make the contradiction clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other source says spices combine even when they come from different prohibitions, such as ערלה and כלאי הכרם, or from different species. חזקיה is about to explain what kind of spices that source means. His explanation is what creates the tension with our משנה. So the actual 'problem' is only finished on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they contrasted them': the גמרא sets two sources against each other
Literally 'names'; here it means separate prohibitions, like ערלה and כלאי הכרם
A species or kind (of plant or food)
They combine to make up the minimum amount

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the contradiction is already complete here. Both sources say spices combine. The real tension appears only once חזקיה's explanation is quoted, on the next amud.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
phrases.notes: This is the usual way the גמרא sets two sources against each other.

phrases.aramaic: תַּבְלִין, שְׁנַיִם וּשְׁלֹשָׁה שֵׁמוֹת מִמִּין אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Spices with two or three prohibitions, from one species,
phrases.notes: For example, some are forbidden as ערלה and others as כלאי הכרם.

phrases.english: or from three species with one prohibition —
are forbidden, and they combine with each other.
phrases.notes: Together they can make up enough to forbid the food they flavor.

phrases.english: And חזקיה said:
phrases.notes: His statement continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It sets an outside source against the משנה line quoted in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that all spices combine for the שבת amount.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A parallel source about forbidden spices also discusses spices combining. חזקיה's explanation of it, quoted next, will limit which spices combine, and that seems to clash with our משנה.
